props.gloss_en: one said: the 'tzela' [from which Eve was built] was a face
and one said: the 'tzela' was a tail
R' Ami: 'behind' (Ps 139:5) -- [last] in the work of creation
R' Ami: 'and before' -- [first] for punishment
(entertained) the punishment in which Adam was first is the punishment after the snake
Rebbi: in [conferring] greatness one begins with the greatest
Rebbi: and in a curse one begins with the least
greatness begins with the greatest -- as it is written, 'and Moses spoke to Aaron and to Elazar and to Itamar, his remaining sons: take...' (Lev 10:12)
a curse begins with the least -- first the snake was cursed, then Eve was cursed, and last Adam was cursed
rather, [Adam was first for] the punishment of the flood
as it is written, 'and He blotted out every living thing on the face of the ground, from man to beast' (Gen 7:23) -- first man, then beast
R' Shimon ben Pazi: [the two yods of vayyitzer say] woe to me from my Creator (yotzri), woe to me from my inclination (yitzri)

R' Abbahu set 'male and female He created them' (Gen 5:2) against 'for in the image of God He made man' (Gen 9:6): how so? at first it arose in [God's] thought to create two, and in the end only one was created
'and He closed up the flesh in its place' (Gen 2:21) was needed only for the place of the incision
R' Shimon ben Menasya: 'and the Lord built the tzela' teaches that the Holy One braided Eve['s hair] and brought her to Adam
for in the coastal towns they call braiding 'binyata' (building)
[ויבן] teaches that the Holy One built Eve like a storehouse: as a storehouse is narrow above and wide below to hold the produce, so a woman is narrow above and wide below to hold the child
'and He brought her to the man' teaches that the Holy One acted as groomsman to Adam
from here the Torah taught proper conduct: a great one should attend a lesser one as groomsman, and not take it ill
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: it is reasonable that the man walked in front [of the two faces]
the baraita: a man should not walk behind a woman on the way, even his own wife
the baraita: if she meets him on a bridge, he should move her to the side
the baraita: whoever passes behind a woman in a river has no portion in the world to come

one who counts coins from his hand into a woman's hand in order to gaze at her, even if he has Torah and good deeds like Moshe our teacher, will not be cleared of the judgement of Gehinnom -- as it is said, 'hand to hand, the evil shall not go unpunished' (Prov 11:21)
Rav Nachman: Manoach was an am haaretz
Rav Nachman's proof-text: 'and Manoach went after his wife' (Judg 13:11)
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: 'went after her' (of Elkana, and of Elisha, II Kings 4:30) means after her words and her counsel -- and here too

Rav Ashi: [on Rav Nachman's view] he had not even read [Scripture] at the schoolhouse -- as it is said, 'and Rivka arose with her maidens, and they rode upon the camels and went after the man' (Gen 24:61) -- and not before the man
R' Yochanan: [better to walk] behind a lion and not behind a woman
R' Yochanan: behind a woman and not behind idolatry
R' Yochanan: behind idolatry and not behind a synagogue when the congregation is praying
we said this only where he carries nothing; if he carries something, there is no concern
only where there is no other entrance; if there is another entrance, there is no concern
only where he is not riding a donkey; if he is riding a donkey, there is no concern
only where he is not wearing tefillin; if he is wearing tefillin, there is no concern

objections.gloss_en: בשלמא למאן דאמר פרצוף, היינו דכתיב אחור וקדם צרתני; אלא למאן דאמר זנב, מאי אחור וקדם צרתני? -- 'You formed me behind and before' (Ps 139:5) fits two faces, not a tail
